chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jumhur, from his father, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was sorrowful and distressed, so he said to me, 'O Sakuni, what has saddened you?'

I said to him, 'A daughter was born to me.' He said to me, 'O Sakuni, the earth bears her weight and Allah provides her sustenance; she will live beyond your lifespan and eat from her own provision.' By Allah, it comforted me, so he said, 'What did you name her?' I said, 'Fatimah.' He said, 'Ahi, Ahi.'

Then he placed his hand on his forehead and said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The right of the child upon the father, if male, is that he exhausts her womb, approves of her name, teaches her the Book of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, purifies her, and teaches her swimming; and if female, he exhausts her womb, approves of her name, teaches her Surah Al-Nur, does not teach her Surah Yusuf (peace be upon him), does not keep her in the upper rooms, and hastens her release to her husband's house.'
As for if you named her Fatimah, do not curse her, do not invoke Allah's displeasure upon her, and do not hit her.'
ai.seo_question: What are the specific rights and duties of a father towards his daughter according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the specific pedagogical and protective duties of fathers, distinguishing between general religious education for boys and the unique emphasis on modesty and early marriage for girls. The Imam’s specific instruction regarding a daughter named Fatimah—avoiding harshness or physical discipline—reflects the reverence for the Prophet’s daughter and serves as a practical model for nurturing female children with gentleness, aligning with the broader Shia emphasis on family dynamics and upbringing.
